_comment: Authoritative pinned commits for every real-world benchmark codebase.
SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Consumed by both:
- playbooks/setup-benchmark-repos.yml  (provisioning: clone + checkout)
- python -m bench corpus-check         (verification: still at the pin?)
Do not duplicate these SHAs anywhere else. Each is the commit its
ground-truth oracle was adjudicated against, so changing one silently
invalidates every ground_truth row for that project (the oracle is keyed
on project+commit+file+line+rule). Re-pin only alongside a re-adjudication.
'name' is also the checkout directory basename and the CODEBASES registry
key in bench/realworld_runner.py -- bench/db.py's result-filename
parsing requires all three to match, which is why pure-ftpd is checked out
as 'pureftpd' (no hyphen).
'scope_include'/'scope_exclude' (task 636): the machine-readable form of
each project's precision_audit/<project>/README.md '## Scope' section --
fnmatch glob lists matched against the project-relative path bench/db.py
already normalizes findings to (project_relpath()). No 'scope_include' key
means unrestricted (whole-repo audit: libcrc only). Include is a
whitelist; exclude further narrows it. 'bench realworld-unlabeled' applies
this by default (see bench/corpus.py:in_scope); pass --no-scope to opt out.
Re-derive from the README, don't hand-edit ad hoc -- these two must stay
in sync (the README is the human-readable rationale, this is what code runs).
GLOB SEMANTICS ARE PATH-AWARE: '*' and '?' and '[...]' stop at '/', and
'**' is what crosses one. So 'src/**' means everything under src/ at any
depth, 'src/*.c' means only the .c files directly in src/, and the two
are NOT the same thing.
This paragraph used to say the opposite -- that these were fnmatch
patterns where '*' crosses '/' -- and that was true when task 636 wrote
the predicate by inheriting fnmatch. benchmarking_db's bench_db/corpus.py
replaced it: fnmatch has no concept of a path, so '*.c' also matched
testes/libs/lib1.c and handed lua five files sqc never scans, overstating
its coverage denominator by 8%. The new predicate was applied to all nine
pinned (project, commit) pairs before the change: eight return a
byte-identical file set and lua drops exactly those five. Nothing was
audited under testes/, so that is a denominator correction only.
raylib is the entry worth naming, because it looks like a break and is
not. It declares 'src/external/*' as an exclude, which under fnmatch was
load-bearing: 'src/*.c' reached into src/external/glfw/... and the exclude
pulled it back out, 121 files -> 23. Under path-aware matching 'src/*.c'
never reaches there, so the exclude is now a no-op -- and the answer is 23
either way. Same set, reached honestly. Keep the exclude regardless: it
still states the intent, and it is what makes the two semantics agree.
A NEW declaration that means 'recursively' must therefore write '**'. One
that writes '*' and means it gets the narrower answer, which is usually
what you want -- and benchmarking_db's assertions check both directions of
drift between what these globs accept and what the runner actually scans
(their tasks 704, 722, 737).
